<FeatureHeader id="fun_battle" />

## What it does

`/battle` (also `/batalha`, `/batalla`) pits two people against each other:
tag two group members, or type `/battle random` to let the bot pick two
members who have spoken in the group before. The bot posts both of their
profile photos side by side with a silly caption — a fight type, a rule and
an "equipment" gag, all randomised — then a real Telegram poll so everyone
can vote on who would win.

## Behaviour that must not change

Two tags, or the word "random" anywhere in the message (which wins even if
two tags are also present), is what triggers a battle; only the first two
tags are ever used. The poll is a genuine Telegram poll — not anonymous, one
vote per person — and nothing in this bot ever closes it; it stays open
until a human does. If fewer than two known members exist for a `"random"`
battle, or a tagged person's photo can't be found, the bot says so instead
of posting anything.

**Not yet ported**: tagging exactly one person, or running `/battle` with no
tag at all, is supposed to pit that person (or you) against a random
"fighter" character image. v1 kept those character images in a private
cloud bucket that was never checked into its own source repository, so
there is nothing to port them from yet — the same blocker
[`fun_death`](/docs/features/fun_death) hit for its own image pool. Until
that's resolved, both of those cases get the same "you need a profile
picture" message v1 already shows when a photo can't be found, rather than
a broken half-feature.

## How to verify it

`qa/features/fun_battle.feature` — six scenarios covering two explicit tags,
`"random"`, the failure paths, and the fun-off gate; run with
`python scripts/cb.py test`. By hand in the sandbox: have two accounts talk
in a group first (so the bot knows who they are), then run
`/battle @name1 @name2` or `/battle random` as anyone in the group and
watch the two photos and the poll arrive together.
